units.title: DC Generator
topics: 1.1. Conservation of Energy, Energy stored in Magnetic Field, Forces and torque in magnetic systems, Singly Excited System. DC Machines & Transformer Course Code: 4332401 above level) Topics and Sub-topics
1.2. Basic principle of DC Generator, Fleming’s right hand rule.
1.3. Various parts of DC generator: yoke, pole core and pole shoes, armature winding, commutators, brushes, lap and wave winding.
1.4. Separately excited, self excited- particularly shunt, series and compound wound type generator.
1.5. E.M.F. equation of generator and various losses in generator.
1.6. No-load, internal and external characteristics
1.7. Applications of DC generator.
uos: 1.a. Understand the principle of Principles of Electromechanical Energy Conversion.
1.b. Explain working principle of DC generator.
1.c. Describe the construction of DC Machines with neat sketches.
1.d. Classify DC generators with neat diagrams.
1.e. Explain the concept of voltage build up and losses.
1.f. Describe various characteristics of DC generator.
1.g. List the applications of DC Generator.

units.title: DC Motor
topics: 2.1. Basic principle of DC motor: Fleming’s left hand rule.
2.2. Back EMF and voltage equation, condition for maximum power, torque relation, shaft torque, relation between torque and speed of motor, losses and efficiency.
2.3. Different characteristics of DC series shunt and compound motor.
2.4. Need of starter in DC motor, three- point, four point starter, supporting conventional resistance and static power electronics converter control.
2.5. Speed control method: armature, field.
uos: 2.a. Explain the working principle of DC motor.
2.b. Describe the concept of back emf, voltage equation, torque, speed, losses and efficiency.
2.c. Describe the behavior of DC series, shunt and compound motor.
2.d. Describe starters used in DC Motor.
2.e. Explain speed control methods of DC Motors.
2.f. List the applications DC Motors. 2.6 General applications of shunt, series, and compound motor.

units.title: 1-Phase Transformer 3.a Explain the working principle of Transformer.
topics: 3.1. Basic principle: Mutual inductance
3.2. EMF equation, voltage and turns ratio. 3.b Understand Construction of 1- phase transformer. 3.c Classify the 1-phase transformers based on different criteria.
3.3. Construction: core type and shell type

3.4. Classification: according to o/p voltage, frequency groups, mode of operations, purpose of usage and according to cooling systems. 3.b Explain the concept of Ideal transformer. 3.c Explain the concept of practical transformer.
3.5. Properties of ideal transformer, Equivalent circuit of ideal transformer.

3.6. Properties of Practical transformer, transformer with winding resistance and leakage reactance. Equivalent circuit of practical transformer. DC Machines & Transformer Course Code: 4332401 above level) Topics and Sub-topics 3.d Perform various tests on transformer.
3.7. Transformer test: Open-circuit (No load test), Short circuit test, Polarity test, load (back to back) test. 3.e Determine the various losses in transformer.
3.8. Transformer losses: Iron (core) loss (hysteresis and eddy current loss), Copper (I2R) loss, stray loss and dielectric loss. 3.f Describe the parallel operation of 1-Phase transformer.
3.9. Parallel operation: reasons and advantages, conditions 3.g Describe operation of 1-phase Variac transformer. 3.h Interpret various parameter of transformer by name plate.
3.10. Variac: working principle, advantages and application.

3.11. Transformer name plate reading includes KVA rating, Voltage Rating, Frequency, Number of Phases, Temperature, Type of Cooling, % Impedance and Reactance, Name of Manufacture, Year of Manufacture.

units.title: 3-Phase and Special types of transformer.
topics: 4.1. Advantages over 3 single phase transformer bank.
4.2. Construction: Core type, Shell type.
4.3. Labeling of transformer terminals.

4.4. 3-Phase transformer connections:  Star-Star: 0º and 180° connections, Problems and solutions.  Delta-Delta: 0º and 180° connections, Advantages and disadvantages.  Star-Delta: ±30°connections, application and advantages  Delta-Star: ±30°connections, application and advantages  Choice of connections: star/star, delta/delta, star/delta.  Scott connection: three phase to two phase conversation and vice versa, applications.  Input-output voltage and current relations for these connections.
4.5. Load test on three phase transformer.
4.6. Pulse transformer: working with input output waveform, application
uos: 4.c. Understand labeling of 3- phase transformer terminals
4.d. Explain the three phase transformer connections with sketches.
4.f. Explain the working of pulse transformer
